packing: Real alpine layers: fleece or light puffer and warm sleep clothes — Theth nights hit the 40s°F in June.
Proper hiking shoes: the Grunas, Blue Eye, and Valbona trails are rocky; trainers are not enough for the pass.
Lek cash: Theth guesthouses, ferries, parking, and bunker museums are cash only.
Sun & water kit: UPF shirts, hats, reef-safe sunscreen, water shoes for pebble beaches, and a dry bag for boat days.
Car & motion kit: nausea meds for the SH21/SH8 switchbacks, snacks, and a phone mount with offline maps.

spots.cost: Cheap and cash-friendly. Bunk’Art 2 about 900 lek (~€9) adult / reduced child; a Bunk’Art 1+2 combo is 1,300 lek (~€13, valid 72h). Skanderbeg Square and Et’hem Bey Mosque are free. A bazaar-grill family dinner runs about 2,500–4,000 lek (~$27–43).
spots.climate: June in Tirana: highs about 78–82°F, lows about 61–66°F, mostly sunny with a chance of an afternoon shower. Perfect for a slow first-evening walk.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the arrival day on foot: Bunk’Art 2, Skanderbeg Square, Et’hem Bey Mosque, and a bazaar-grill dinner are all a few minutes apart. Withdraw lek from an ATM (choose “without conversion”) — the bunker museums and market stalls are cash only.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the Dajti Ekspres cable car (~1,500 lek / €15 round trip, 15 min each way) — but note it is CLOSED on Tuesdays, which is arrival day, so schedule it for a different Tirana touch or skip it.
spots.restoHtml:
• Zgara te Pazari — classic bazaar grill; plain grilled chicken / qofte + fries is the safest picky-kid table in town, cheap and fast
  • Era — long-running crowd-pleaser doing Albanian plus pizza and pasta; the reliable “everyone finds something” fallback
  • Oda — atmospheric traditional room by the bazaar (tave kosi, fergese, grills); order kids the grilled chicken + bread + fries
spots.altboxHtml:
• Dajti Ekspres cable car for an effortless mountain-top panorama — only on a non-Tuesday.
  • Pyramid of Tirana, now a walkable stepped park, is a good sunset landmark a short stroll away.
  • Bunk’Art 1 (the huge 5-story bunker at the Dajti edge) if you want the deeper Cold-War museum on a fuller, non-arrival day.

spots.cost: Rozafa Castle entry is a few hundred lek per adult (~€3–5), kids reduced. A lakeside lunch for four runs roughly €30–50. This is a half-day stop on the drive up, not a paid-attraction day.
spots.climate: Warm lowland stop before the mountains: June highs in the low 80s°F. Golden hour on the castle walls over Lake Shkodra and the Buna/Drin confluence is the photo.
spots.saveHtml: Save Stretch the legs at Rozafa Castle and grab a lakeside fish lunch, then push on to Theth. Fill the fuel tank in Koplik — there is no petrol station in Theth.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge If you leave Tirana early, a short Lake Shkodra boat spin or a stop at the Ottoman Mesi Bridge makes the transition day its own small adventure.
spots.restoHtml:
• Shiroka lakeside restaurants — grilled lake fish, plus pasta, fries, and grilled chicken for the kids
  • Shkoder center pizzerias — the pedestrian café street has easy wood-fired pizza before the mountain leg
spots.altboxHtml:
• Mesi Bridge (Ottoman stone arch) for a quick photogenic leg-stretch north of town.
  • Lake Shkodra shore for a swim or bike if the day is running ahead of schedule.
  • Venice Art Mask Factory if a rain shower interrupts the outdoor plan.

days.travelNote: Travel day into the mountains — Shkoder is the gateway stop, Theth is the destination.

days.heading: Theth on foot
days.note: Ease into the mountains with the valley’s best easy hike, the postcard church, and the blood-feud lock-in tower — a full day without a hard climb.

spots.name: Grunas Waterfall — the best family hike from the village
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · grunaswaterfallIG · thethIG · albanianalpsFlickr

images.alt: Grunas Waterfall over mossy rock
images.captionTitle: Grunas Waterfall over mossy rock

images.alt: Grunas cascade in Theth National Park
images.captionTitle: Grunas cascade in Theth National Park

spots.cost: Free (national-park land). This is a no-ticket day — just water, snacks, and good shoes.
spots.climate: Easy-to-moderate, ~2.5 km each way, 2–3 hr round trip with kids. Flat riverside start, then a ~200 m climb with one steep final section. Well within an 8-year-old’s ability with breaks.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk straight from the Theth church; no guide or transport needed. Pair it with the village church and the lock-in tower for a full, low-cost first mountain day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Grab byrek and fresh trout at a trailside guesthouse café on the way back instead of self-catering.
spots.restoHtml:
• Your guesthouse half-board dinner — the default and usually excellent: bread, byrek, pasta, grilled meat, fresh dairy; tell the host about dislikes and they accommodate
  • Village guesthouse cafés — simple omelets, fries, and byrek for lunch between hikes
spots.altboxHtml:
• Kulla e Ngujimit (lock-in tower) — the blood-feud refuge tower, now a tiny museum (~150 lek); the “castle where the men hid” framing lands with both kids.
  • Theth church meadow at golden hour for the postcard shot of the whole region.
  • Riverside picnic below the village if legs are tired after the drive in.

spots.cost: Village wandering is free. The Kulla e Ngujimit (lock-in tower) museum is about 150 lek (~$1.50); locals from the next house open it on request. Guesthouse half-board runs roughly €20–35 per person.
spots.climate: Theth sits at 770 m: June valley highs ~73°F, but nights are genuinely cold (~46–54°F) and the pass is colder. Pack real layers and warm sleep clothes. Afternoon thunderstorms are the operative hazard.
spots.saveHtml: Save The church, the meadows, and the stone kulla towers cost nothing and are the visual heart of the valley — shoot them at golden hour.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A local guide for a half-day of valley history and the Kanun (mountain-law) code turns the towers from photo stops into a story.
spots.restoHtml:
• Guesthouse family dinner — set, multi-course, home-cooked (often with house wine and welcome raki); the best food in the valley
  • Bujtina Polia — the best-documented Theth bujtina; hearty half-board with plenty of plain options for kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Grunas Waterfall if you have not already done it — the natural companion to a village day.
  • Blue Eye of Theth as a half-day if weather closes the higher trails.
  • Slow recovery day — the valley rewards doing less; read in the meadow before the big pass day.

days.heading: Blue Eye of Theth

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Drive to Nderlysaj + ~2 hr round-trip walk

facts.label: Water
facts.valueHtml: Crystal-clear and frigid — a quick plunge

days.note: The recovery day opposite the big pass hike: the drive-and-walk version of the northern Blue Eye is easy enough for the 8-year-old and dramatic enough for everyone.

spots.name: Blue Eye of Theth (Syri i Kalter) — the turquoise spring
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · blueeyeofthethIG · syrikalterIG · thethFlickr

images.alt: Turquoise pool below a Theth cascade
images.captionTitle: Turquoise pool below a Theth cascade

images.alt: Crystal-clear forest stream, Theth
images.captionTitle: Crystal-clear forest stream, Theth

spots.cost: The pool itself is free. The family-smart version: drive to Nderlysaj, then a ~4.8 km / ~2-hour round-trip walk. Budget a few euros for parking / a short 4x4 shuttle segment at the trailhead (not consistently posted).
spots.climate: Glacial and crystal-clear — and frigid (~50–55°F) year-round. Expect a brief, shrieky plunge, not a lazy swim. This is the northern Theth Blue Eye — a different place from the famous southern one near Sarande.
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip the full 11 km hike from the village; the Nderlysaj drive-and-walk gives the same payoff at a fraction of the effort — ideal as the recovery day opposite the big pass hike.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Hire a village 4x4 shuttle for the rough final stretch so the 8-year-old saves energy for the walk to the pool.
spots.restoHtml:
• Nderlysaj trailhead cafés — byrek, omelets, fries, and grilled trout right by the parking
  • Back at your Theth guesthouse for the half-board dinner — no need to seek out a restaurant
spots.altboxHtml:
• Grunas Waterfall if you want a second easy water hike the same day.
  • Kulla lock-in tower on the way back for a short cultural stop.
  • Village downtime — the cold plunge plus the walk is a full, satisfying day for younger legs.

days.heading: Valbona Pass day
days.feel: The epic — full crossing or turn-back

facts.label: Default
facts.valueHtml: Out-and-back to the meadows / first viewpoint

facts.label: Upgrade
facts.valueHtml: Full crossing with guide + mule, off the col by 2 pm

days.note: The signature Balkan day-hike — honestly framed. The 8-year-old is the limiting factor, so the default is a turn-back with the same big views; the full ~1,800 m crossing is a conscious upgrade with a guide and a mule.

spots.name: Valbona Pass — the epic (with a kid-friendly turn-back)
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · valbonapassIG · thethtovalbonaIG · accursedmountainsFlickr

images.alt: Accursed Mountains at sunset over Valbona
images.captionTitle: Accursed Mountains at sunset over Valbona

images.alt: Lone hiker on a Valbona ridge trail
images.captionTitle: Lone hiker on a Valbona ridge trail

images.alt: Limestone peaks of Valbona National Park
images.captionTitle: Limestone peaks of Valbona National Park

spots.cost: The trail is free. Families add a mule + handler (arranged the night before through your guesthouse; luggage-mule ~$25–45/bag, a child-carry/porter arrangement negotiated above that) and often a local guide (~€70–100 pp, sometimes bundling transport).
spots.climate: ~16–17 km point-to-point, ~1,000 m climb out of Theth, 7–9 hr total, over the ~1,800 m col. Moderate-to-challenging — explicitly not a casual family walk.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do it as an out-and-back from Theth, turning around at the tree-line meadows or the first mountain café on the ascent. You get the dramatic valley views without committing the 8-year-old to a 9-hour crossing.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge For the full one-way crossing, book a guide and a mule: hike Theth → Valbona, then loop back scenically via the Koman Lake ferry rather than backtracking. Be at/past the pass by 2 pm — afternoon storms are common, forcing a 6–7 am start.
spots.restoHtml:
• Guesthouse packed lunch — arrange it the night before; there is little on the trail beyond a seasonal café or two
  • Rilindja (Valbona side) — the institution at the far end if you do the full crossing
spots.altboxHtml:
• Turn-back at the first viewpoint — the honest default with an 8-year-old; nobody regrets the meadows.
  • Mule for the kids on the ascent so the family can go higher together.
  • Swap for a Koman ferry day entirely if early-June snow still sits on the col (verify with your guesthouse a few days out).

days.heading: Koman Lake ferry

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Drive to Koman, ferry the canyon, swim the Shala

facts.label: Note
facts.valueHtml: Verify summer sailing times; book ahead

days.note: The scenic counterpoint to all the hiking: a ferry through a fjord-like canyon, plus a Shala River swim stop that the kids will rank as the trip highlight.

spots.name: Koman Lake ferry — the fjord-canyon boat day
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · komanlakeIG · komanferryIG · shalaFlickr

images.alt: Koman Lake between sheer fjord walls
images.captionTitle: Koman Lake between sheer fjord walls

images.alt: The ferry threading the Koman canyon
images.captionTitle: The ferry threading the Koman canyon

images.alt: Clear blue water ringed by mountains, Koman
images.captionTitle: Clear blue water ringed by mountains, Koman

spots.cost: Foot passengers ~€8–11 pp (family of four ~€32–44); vehicles priced by size. Berisha runs the big car-and-passenger ferry, typically Koman 09:00 out / return early afternoon — verify seasonally and book ahead in summer.
spots.climate: A ~2.5–3 hr ride through a fjord-like canyon: vertical limestone walls dropping into deep turquoise-green water, road-less hamlets, snow-dusted peaks behind. Regularly called one of the world’s most beautiful boat rides.
spots.saveHtml: Save As a Theth-based day, drive to Koman, ride out and back, and skip the vehicle fee by going on foot. Many trips add a side run up the Shala River (“Albania’s Thailand”) for a pool-blue swim — an easy crowd-pleaser for kids.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a Shala River boat excursion with a swim stop and lunch — the highlight of the ferry day for the 8-year-old.
spots.restoHtml:
• Shala River eco-restaurants — grilled fish and simple plates at the swim beaches
  • Koman-side cafés — basic byrek, fries, and drinks by the dock before/after
spots.altboxHtml:
• Full Valbona crossing loop — use the ferry (Fierze→Koman) as the scenic exit from a one-way pass hike.
  • Shala River swim day if the family wants water over another long hike.
  • Recovery in Theth if the pass day was tiring — the ferry is optional, not mandatory.

days.heading: The big drive to the Riviera

facts.label: Reveal
facts.valueHtml: Llogara Pass opens the whole turquoise coast

days.note: One deliberate scenic driving day down the length of the country. Leave Theth by ~07:00; take the Llogara tunnel when tired, or the old pass road for the view. First Ionian swim at Dhermi optional.

spots.name: Llogara Pass & the Riviera reveal
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · llogarapassIG · dhermiIG · albanianrivieraFlickr

images.alt: Llogara Pass vista over the Riviera
images.captionTitle: Llogara Pass vista over the Riviera

images.captionTitle: Dhermi white village above the turquoise shore

images.captionTitle: Aerial of the Dhermi coastline

spots.cost: The drive is the attraction — free. Budget only fuel and a lunch stop. The Llogara tunnel (~7 min) saves time on a long transfer day; the old pass road (30+ min of hairpins) trades time for one of the great sea-and-mountain views in the Balkans.
spots.climate: The big transfer day: Theth → Ksamil is ~415 km and a realistic 8–9 hr with stops. The reward is the moment the road crests Llogara and the whole turquoise Riviera opens below at Dhermi.
spots.saveHtml: Save Take the tunnel on the way down when everyone is tired; leave Theth by ~07:00 and treat this as one deliberate scenic driving day rather than squeezing a hike in first.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Take the old pass road for the viewpoint and a coffee at the top, then drop into Dhermi for a first Ionian swim before the final push to Ksamil.
spots.restoHtml:
• Llogara pass grills — spit-roast lamb and simple plates with a view; fries and bread for kids
  • Dhermi beach pizzerias — first-swim lunch on the coast
spots.altboxHtml:
• Split the drive with a night in Berat or Vlore if 8–9 hours in a day is too much (see the Status card).
  • First swim at Dhermi to break up the descent.
  • Vlore waterfront stop for a leg-stretch and ice cream before the coastal road.

days.heading: Ksamil beaches & islets

facts.label: Water
facts.valueHtml: ~72-75°F, calm, clear — warm enough to laze in

facts.label: Kids
facts.valueHtml: Wade / swim to the offshore islets

days.note: The reason the swim leg beats an Atlantic island: warm, calm, turquoise water and little islets the 8-year-old can reach on their own. Unpack once and settle in.

spots.name: Ksamil beaches & islets — the swim payoff
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · ksamilIG · ksamilislandsIG · albanianrivieraFlickr

images.alt: Ksamil islet ringed by turquoise water

spots.cost: Two sunbeds + umbrella run ~1,500–2,000 lek (€15–20 / $16–21) a day in June (cash). A motorboat taxi to the islets is ~500–1,000 lek/person; pedalos ~€20/hr. The beaches themselves are free to walk onto.
spots.climate: June air highs ~83°F; Ionian sea ~72°F rising into the mid-70s by late June. Genuinely warm, calm, and Caribbean-clear — the warm-water swim a Madeira/Atlantic trip cannot match. Water is clearest in the morning.
spots.saveHtml: Save Base here so you unpack once. Swim or wade to the little offshore islets — shallow and safe for the 8-year-old — instead of paying for a boat every day. Try Mirror Beach (Pasqyra) or Pulebardha for clearer, less-mobbed water.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A half-day motorboat rental to the islets, or a beach club with front-row loungers on a peak afternoon.
spots.restoHtml:
• Abiori Bar Restaurant Pizzeria — on the sand, wood-fired pizza and pasta for the kids
  • Fourth Island — garden terrace; pizza, pasta, salads plus grilled fish
  • The Mussel House — Lake Butrint mussels for the adults, pasta and cake for the kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Mirror Beach (Pasqyra) ~10 min away for clearer water and fewer crowds.
  • Pulebardha cove for snorkeling off the rocks.
  • Sunset xhiro in Sarande (~20 min) for the waterfront promenade and ice cream.

days.heading: Butrint, then the beach

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: Butrint ruins loop, 9-11 am to beat the heat

days.note: The one culture day on the coast, timed early against the June sun — a Greek theatre, Venetian tower, and climbable walls in a forest — then straight back to the water.

spots.name: Butrint National Park (UNESCO) — ruins in the forest
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · butrintIG · butrintnationalparkIG · unescoFlickr

images.alt: Ancient stone gate in the Butrint forest
images.captionTitle: Ancient stone gate in the Butrint forest

images.alt: Weathered columns at Butrint
images.captionTitle: Weathered columns at Butrint

images.alt: Pulebardha cove inside Butrint NP
images.captionTitle: Pulebardha cove inside Butrint NP

spots.cost: Adult 1,000 lek (~€10); child 6–12 500 lek (~€5); under 6 free (cash preferred). A 2–3 hr flat woodland loop, ~15 min south of Ksamil.
spots.climate: Wooded but sun-exposed at the ruins. June midday is intense — go 9–11 am or after 4 pm, bring water and real shoes, then swim back in Ksamil in the afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Go early to beat both the heat and the tour buses, then bank the rest of the day for the beach. No guide needed — the signage and layout do the work.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A licensed guide brings the Greek theatre, the Lion Gate, and the Venetian tower alive for the 13-year-old.
spots.restoHtml:
• The Mussel House — on the Lake Butrint waterfront between the ruins and Ksamil; easy lunch stop
  • Ksamil pizzerias — back in town for the picky-kid default after the ruins
spots.altboxHtml:
• Climbable city walls + Venetian tower — the “treasure hunt in the forest” that keeps kids moving.
  • Turtles in the ponds and the carved Lion Gate for the 8-year-old.
  • Afternoon Ksamil swim to cool off after the ruins.

days.heading: The wild north coast

facts.label: Swim
facts.valueHtml: Porto Palermo’s calm bay is the kid win

days.note: A day trip to the quieter, wilder Riviera: the canyon-mouth cove at Gjipe (by boat for the kids), Himare’s beaches, and Porto Palermo’s castle and glass-clear bay.

spots.name: The wild north coast: Himare, Gjipe & Porto Palermo
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · himaraIG · gjipeIG · portopalermoFlickr

images.alt: Aerial of the Sarande–Riviera coast
images.captionTitle: Aerial of the Sarande–Riviera coast

images.alt: Rocky Ionian shoreline near Sarande
images.captionTitle: Rocky Ionian shoreline near Sarande

spots.cost: A day trip up the SH8 (~1h20 to Himare). Porto Palermo castle 300 lek (~€3); Gjipe clifftop parking 300 lek; a Gjipe boat taxi from Himare ~€15–20 pp. Himare sunbeds ~€10–20.
spots.climate: The quieter, wilder Riviera. Gjipe is a pebble cove at a canyon mouth walled by ~20 m cliffs; Porto Palermo has one of the calmest, glass-clear bays on the coast — gentle entry, ideal for kids.
spots.saveHtml: Save Reach Gjipe by the clifftop park-and-walk (30–45 min down, unshaded) only if everyone is up for the hot climb back; otherwise it is a scenery day at Himare’s Livadhi and Llamani beaches. Bring your own water — Gjipe has none.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Take the boat taxi to Gjipe from Himare so the 8-year-old skips the brutal uphill return, and add Porto Palermo’s Ali Pasha castle + calm-bay swim on the way back.
spots.restoHtml:
• Pizzeria Napoli, Himare — straightforward pizza and pasta
  • Obelix Beer N’ Burger — burgers and fries for a guaranteed kid win
spots.altboxHtml:
• Porto Palermo bay — the calmest, kid-friendliest swim on the whole coast, with a castle to explore (bring a flashlight for the dungeons).
  • Livadhi & Llamani beaches at Himare if the Gjipe walk or boat does not line up.
  • Dhermi for a livelier beach scene on the way back south.

days.heading: Blue Eye + boat day
days.feel: Juneteenth observed: a no-PTO water day

facts.label: Plan
facts.valueHtml: Blue Eye of Sarande morning + boat or town evening

days.note: Juneteenth (observed) lands mid-trip as a free active day. Pair the cheap, dramatic Blue Eye of Sarande with a boat trip to the sea caves or a Sarande waterfront evening.

spots.name: Blue Eye of Sarande + a boat day
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · blueeyesarandeIG · syrikalterIG · sarandeFlickr

images.alt: The turquoise Blue Eye spring of Sarande
images.captionTitle: The turquoise Blue Eye spring of Sarande

spots.cost: Blue Eye entry is almost nothing — 50 lek/person, 100 lek/car, parking 200–800 lek. A shared boat trip from Ksamil/Sarande runs €16–37 pp; a 3-hour RIB to Tongo Island with snorkel gear is ~€60 pp (family of four ~€240).
spots.climate: A vivid turquoise-to-emerald karst spring, ~50–54°F and look-don’t-swim (cold and officially protected — people dip downstream). An easy ~2 km flat, shaded forest walk to the boardwalk; go before 9 am in peak.
spots.saveHtml: Save Pair the Blue Eye (a cheap 2–3 hr morning stop) with a Sarande waterfront evening — both low-cost. Skip the pricey private boat and take a shared “Five Islands” circuit if you want time on the water.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A half-day RIB boat to the sea caves and Tongo Island with snorkeling — the trip highlight for water-loving kids.
spots.restoHtml:
• Sarande waterfront (Hasan Tahsini) — al-fresco dining with pizza/pasta options and the evening promenade
  • Veranda Apollonia, Ksamil — rooftop sea views; pizza, risotto, grilled fish
spots.altboxHtml:
• Shared boat trip to the coves and sea caves instead of a private charter.
  • Sarande city beach + xhiro for a low-key town evening.

What to lock, watch, and expect

Current research refreshed July 2026 for a June 2027 trip. Kids assumed 13 and 8.

Solid

The concept is coherent

Theth delivers the alpine epic and dramatically different scenery; Ksamil delivers the warm-water swim. It is a genuine Madeira upgrade, not a lateral move.

Depart Mon Jun 7, ferry to Corfu Jun 20, fly home Jun 21, arrive by Jun 22. No travel on Jun 23-26.

The budget has huge headroom

The Valbona pass vs an 8-year-old

The full crossing is 7-9 hr over a 1,800 m col — a real stretch for the 8-year-old. Default to the out-and-back; treat the full crossing as a guided, mule-assisted upgrade.

The Valbona pass is snow-closed until roughly early-to-mid June; Jun 9-13 is usually walkable but at the boundary. Verify with the guesthouse a few days out and keep a Grunas/Koman fallback.

~415 km, a realistic 8-9 hr. Plan it as one deliberate scenic day (early start, Llogara tunnel when tired) or split it with a Berat/Vlore night.

Travel Tips

The stuff nobody tells you

Operational rules that keep a two-region Albania route smooth with kids.

Book in roughly this order

  1. Open-jaw PIT-Tirana / Corfu-PIT airfare · start tracking when schedules load
  2. Theth guesthouse (half-board) and Ksamil apartment · refundable, family rooms
  3. Rental car with free one-way drop, automatic · TIA pickup, Sarande drop
  4. Sarande-Corfu ferry + Corfu buffer hotel · once flight home is set
  5. Valbona guide/mule, Koman & sea-cave boats · nearer the date, weather-dependent

Cash & currency

Albania runs on lek

  • Carry lek cash — Theth guesthouses, ferries, parking, bunker museums, and market stalls are cash only.
  • Withdraw “without conversion” at ATMs to dodge DCC fees.
  • Euros work poorly on the coast — you’ll lose on the rate.

The mountains

Scale the big hike honestly

  • The full Valbona pass is not a casual family walk. Default to a turn-back with the 8-year-old.
  • Verify snow on the col a few days out; keep a Grunas/Koman fallback.
  • Pack real layers — Theth nights hit the 40s°F even in June.

The drive

Respect the transfer day

  • Theth -> Ksamil is 8-9 hr. Leave by 07:00 or split with a Berat/Vlore night.
  • Take the Llogara tunnel when everyone is tired; the old pass road for the view.
  • No night driving on the winding, unlit SH8 coast road.

The coast

Warm water, easy wins

  • Mornings are clearest at Ksamil; sheltered coves stagnate by afternoon.
  • Butrint early (9-11 am) to beat heat and buses, then swim.
  • Gjipe by boat with kids — the uphill return is brutal in the sun.

What People Are Saying

Research signals to keep in mind

Guidebooks, road-trip write-ups, and official pages agree on the shape of this trip: north for the hiking, south for the swimming, and a ferry — not a flight — to leave.

Mountains signal

The Theth-Valbona pass is repeatedly called one of the best day-hikes in the Balkans, and the Koman ferry one of the world’s most scenic boat rides — the reasons the north is worth five nights.

Coast signal

Ksamil’s water is described as Caribbean-grade, warm and clear by mid-June, with wade-able islets — exactly the family swim payoff the Madeira idea lacked.

Logistics signal

The recurring advice: one rental car north-to-south, drop it in Sarande, and ferry to Corfu to fly home. No island-hop, no self-transfer risk.
